TL;DR for attackers
Kerberos is the default AD auth protocol; most lateral-movement chains will touch it. For handsâon cheatsheets (ASâREP/Kerberoasting, ticket forging, delegation abuse, etc.) see:
88tcp/udp - Pentesting Kerberos
Fresh attack notes (2024â2026)
RC4 finally going away
â Windows Server 2025 DCs no longer issue RC4 TGTs; Microsoft plans to disable RC4 as default for AD DCs by end of Q2 2026. Environments that reâenable RC4 for legacy apps create downgrade/fastâcrack opportunities for Kerberoasting.
PAC validation enforcement (Apr 2025)
â April 2025 updates remove âCompatibilityâ mode; forged PACs/golden tickets get rejected on patched DCs when enforcement is enabled. Legacy/unpatched DCs remain abusable.
CVEâ2025â26647 (altSecID CBA mapping)
â If DCs are unpatched or left in Audit mode, certificates chained to nonâNTAuth CAs but mapped via SKI/altSecID can still log on. Events 45/21 appear when protections trigger.
NTLM phaseâout
â Microsoft will ship future Windows releases with NTLM disabled by default (staged through 2026), pushing more auth to Kerberos. Expect more Kerberos surface area and stricter EPA/CBT in hardened networks.
Crossâdomain RBCD remains powerful
â Microsoft Learn notes that resourceâbased constrained delegation works across domains/forests; writable
msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity
on resource objects still allows S4U2selfâS4U2proxy impersonation without touching frontâend service ACLs.
Quick tooling
Rubeus kerberoast (AES default)
:
Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:svc_sql /aes /nowrap /outfile:tgs.txt
â outputs AES hashes; plan for GPU cracking or target preâauth disabled users instead.
RC4 downgrade target hunting
: enumerate accounts that still advertise RC4 with
Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes=4)' -Properties msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes
to locate weak kerberoast candidates before RC4 is fully disabled.
